approach: Use the x-motion to find the time when x = 29 m, then substitute that time into the y-motion and the velocity components.

steps.text: Write x(t) using zero initial x-velocity and aₓ = 4.0 m/s².
Set x(t) = 29 m and solve for t.
Write y(t) using initial y-velocity 8.0 m/s and a_y = 2.0 m/s², then substitute t.
Find the velocity components at this time and combine them for the speed.

common_mistakes.text: Writing x(t) = aₓt² instead of ½aₓt², dropping the one-half factor, gives t ≈ 2.69 s and y ≈ 28.8 m, both wrong.
